independence: Hand-authored XML plus separately authored explicit timeline equations; no production imports or parser reuse.
assertionPolicy: Expected objects are recursive projections. Compare provided scalar fields and complete provided event arrays; requiredCodes must be present and forbiddenCodes absent in measure findings. Unspecified fields are unconstrained.

cases.description: Four quarter notes in 4/4
cases.rationale: Four durations of 4 divisions / 4 divisions per quarter = 4 quarters.

cases.description: Twelve triplet eighths, duration 4 / divisions 12
cases.rationale: Twelve exact thirds total four; time-modification must not scale encoded duration a second time.

cases.description: A shorter chord tone is allowed and does not move the cursor
cases.rationale: The chord member shares onset zero, ends at one, and the next non-chord note starts at two.

cases.description: A chord tone longer than its anchor is reported
cases.rationale: The chord violates MusicXML's anchor-duration restriction but cannot move the cursor to two.

cases.description: Two voices occupy the same four-quarter measure
cases.rationale: Parallel voices have eight quarters of summed note durations but only four quarters of measure extent.

cases.description: A partial second voice can finish before the measure extent
cases.rationale: The first voice reaches four. A final cursor of three is not evidence of an underfilled measure.

cases.description: Backup crosses measure start by exactly 1/12 quarter
cases.rationale: One minus thirteen twelfths is negative one twelfth. No float tolerance or clamp may erase it.

cases.description: A whole-measure rest occupies three quarters in 3/4
cases.rationale: The encoded duration 72 / 24 wins over the whole-rest glyph; a 3/4 whole-measure rest lasts three quarters.

cases.description: Additive numerator 3+2/8
cases.rationale: (3+2) times 4/8 quarters per eighth note = 5/2 quarters.

cases.description: Composite meter 2/4 + 3/8
cases.rationale: Independent beat-type pairs sum to 2 + 3/2 = 7/2 quarters.

cases.description: Decimal duration .1 and divisions .3 preserve exact thirds
cases.rationale: (.1/.3) + (.1/.3) + (.1/.3) is exactly one, not an approximate decimal.

cases.description: A grace-note chord has zero encoded duration
cases.rationale: Grace and grace-chord events do not advance the encoded musical position.

cases.description: An implicit pickup is surfaced without a false underfull finding
cases.rationale: Implicit can mark a pickup or split repeat. Its short duration is review context, not automatically an error.

cases.description: Mid-measure divisions invalidate timing until restored at a boundary
cases.rationale: The tool deliberately does not interpret mid-measure divisions. That uncertainty must survive inheritance and end only at an explicit supported boundary.

cases.description: Mid-measure time invalidates expected length while exact duration remains available
cases.rationale: Known divisions still support exact event positions; no trusted target meter exists until a supported boundary time signature restores it.

cases.description: Repeated and nonnumeric measure labels preserve ordinal identity
cases.rationale: Three source measures remain three rows. A label is not a unique key; attributes also inherit across boundaries.

cases.description: A measure ends exactly 1/12 quarter short
cases.rationale: The deficit is 1 - 11/12 = 1/12, exactly.

cases.description: A measure ends exactly 1/12 quarter long
cases.rationale: The excess is 13/12 - 1 = 1/12, exactly.

cases.description: Cue notes carry encoded duration
cases.rationale: Cue appearance is not grace timing: an ordinary cue note advances the position by its duration.

cases.description: A shorter intermediate chord tone does not change the original anchor
cases.rationale: Both chord tones use the first preceding non-chord note's two-quarter duration and onset.

cases.description: Forward contributes to the occupied encoded timeline
cases.rationale: A silent forward of sixteen divisions advances the four-quarter timeline without requiring a note.

cases.description: Division integers above IEEE-754 safe integer stay exact
cases.rationale: A one-division deficit remains visible even when both lexical integers exceed Number's exactness boundary.
